boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Mississippi State traditions, from the ringing cowbell to spring homecoming.

cards.title: Ring the Cowbell
cards.subtitle: Bulldog athletic tradition
cards.notes: Bring or photograph a cowbell at an MSU athletic setting, and follow venue and conference guidance on when ringing is permitted.
cards.short_summary: MSU identifies the cowbell as its longstanding visual and auditory symbol of pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State says students began bringing cowbells to outdoor athletic events and that the tradition continues today.
cards.access_notes: Use only where event and venue policies permit; the source describes the tradition, not public access or pricing.

cards.title: Start the Season at Cowbell Yell
cards.subtitle: Football-season kickoff pep rally
cards.notes: Watch the Student Association’s announcements for the next Cowbell Yell, then attend the pep rally to learn the traditions presented there.
cards.short_summary: A Student Association and Athletics pep rally that introduces traditions and supports the football team.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU’s Student Association describes Cowbell Yell as a co-sponsored event that teaches new students traditions and kicks off football season.
cards.source_title: Cowbell Yell | Mississippi State University Student Association
cards.access_notes: The Student Association states that Cowbell Yell is open to students, faculty, staff, fans, and community members; confirm the current event details.

cards.title: Learn “Hail State”
cards.subtitle: Mississippi State fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at an official MSU event and use the university’s published lyrics to recognize the refrain and school call.
cards.short_summary: The official fight song gives Mississippi State’s game-day call a shared soundtrack.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State publishes “Hail State” as its fight song and provides its lyrics on the traditions page.
cards.source_title: Hail State Fight Song | Mississippi State University
cards.access_notes: The source documents the song; event attendance and access vary by venue.

cards.title: Join the Maroon & White Cheer
cards.subtitle: School colors and game-day cheer
cards.notes: Wear maroon and white for an MSU game or campus event, then listen for the published Maroon and White Cheer during play.
cards.short_summary: The school colors trace to MSU’s first football game and remain part of its game-day cheer.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU states that maroon and white date to its first football game in 1895 and that the Bulldog Family shouts the Maroon and White Cheer at games.
cards.access_notes: The source describes the colors and cheer; game admission and event access vary.

cards.title: Wear Maroon on Friday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Bulldog-pride practice
cards.notes: On a Friday, add at least one maroon item to your outfit and photograph the color tradition in an appropriate campus setting.
cards.short_summary: Bulldogs mark every Friday by wearing maroon.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State says Bulldogs around the world wear at least one piece of maroon clothing each Friday of the year.
cards.access_notes: This is a voluntary apparel tradition; no event admission is described.

cards.title: Catch Bulldog Bash
cards.subtitle: Fall outdoor concert tradition
cards.notes: Check the official event announcement for the current lineup and location, then attend the outdoor concert with your group.
cards.short_summary: Bulldog Bash is MSU’s fall concert tradition held before an SEC home football game.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State describes Bulldog Bash as Mississippi’s largest free outdoor concert, held on a fall-semester Friday night before an SEC home football game.
cards.access_notes: The university describes Bulldog Bash as free; confirm the current date, location, and any event rules before attending.

cards.title: Begin with Dawg Days
cards.subtitle: New-student welcome tradition
cards.notes: If you are an incoming freshman or transfer student, use the Dawg Days schedule to choose activities that help you learn campus.
cards.short_summary: A two-week collection of activities designed to help new Bulldogs get acclimated.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU describes Dawg Days as activities and events during the two weeks before fall classes for incoming freshmen and transfer students.
cards.access_notes: Designed for incoming freshmen and transfer students; consult current university programming for participation details.

cards.title: Return for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Fall-semester alumni and student gathering
cards.notes: Review the official homecoming schedule when released, then choose a campus event or football-related activity that fits your visit.
cards.short_summary: MSU frames its fall homecoming as a reunion for alumni, friends, Starkville, and the Bulldog Family.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State says Homecoming is held each fall semester and brings alumni and friends back to campus for a football game and celebration.
cards.access_notes: Events and football-game admission vary; check the current university and athletics schedules.

cards.title: See Spring Homecoming in Motion
cards.subtitle: Super Bulldog Weekend
cards.notes: Use the official weekend schedule to pick an activity, such as the spring football scrimmage or an alumni event, before making plans.
cards.short_summary: MSU’s spring homecoming combines athletics, alumni programming, and related campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: MSU Alumni describes Super Bulldog Weekend as spring semester’s version of fall homecoming, including baseball, a maroon-white football scrimmage, alumni events, and more.
cards.access_notes: Individual activities may have separate access requirements or tickets; consult the current schedule.

cards.title: Spot the Costume Bully
cards.subtitle: Official university mascot tradition
cards.notes: Look for the shaggy tan Bully costume mascot at an official campus or athletic event, and take a photo only when event staff allow.
cards.short_summary: Students portray Bully at university functions and selected home athletic events.
cards.evidence_claim: Mississippi State says around five students each year wear the Bully costume for Alumni Association functions and pre-game home football and basketball events.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances depend on official event programming; respect staff direction and photo policies.
